text:
DONE. Absorbs P7.5 (bd-01KYNA5EPTP9Y8QAH1673G613D), which covered only the agent<->client wire and never reached this.

A CallFailure algebra now sits between AgentFailure and the scheduler outcome, classifying what a failed call actually ESTABLISHES rather than what shape it happened to arrive in:

  NotStarted(kind, code)      the remote agent never ran; safely repeatable
  TransportLost(afterWrite)   the connection broke; afterWrite decides whether it may have acted
  RemoteReported(code)        the exchange completed and the far side reported failure, so it DID run
  ResponseUntrusted(code)     the exchange completed but the answer could not be trusted

The old code collapsed all seven AgentFailure variants into SpawnFailed(Unknown), which asserted three things at once: that the remote program never ran, that nothing is known about why, and — for RemoteCliFailure, RemoteAgentFailure and ProtocolViolation, which arise ONLY after a successful exchange — a plain falsehood.

Three behavioural fixes fall out, each with a property:

1. AgentUnavailable now maps to SpawnFailureKind.ExecutableMissing and AuthenticationFailed to PermissionDenied. Those kinds existed in the kernel and nothing ever produced them.
2. A ProtocolViolation on submit is now AcceptanceUnknown(ResponseUnparseable), not InvocationFailed. It reaches the client on a zero-exit ssh, so the request WAS delivered — reporting it as a definite non-submission was the same false-certainty defect as A4, one layer up. ResponseUnparseable already existed and the CLI backend already used it; only the SSH path lied.
3. The submit and cancel laws are now expressed by ONE predicate, mayHaveActed, instead of a hardcoded TransportDisconnected(true, _, _) pattern in each. That is why the fix generalizes: A3 made cancellation honest for transport loss specifically, and D5 makes both operations honest for every failure that could have taken effect.

An unparseable response is also no longer reported as a transport interruption, so "the wire broke" and "the agent answered something unreadable" stay distinguishable.

The superseded agentFailureCode string-mapper was deleted; codes now come from the classification, so a variant cannot acquire a code without a decision about what it establishes.

Verification: 3 new properties (7 total in UncertaintyLawSuite, up from 4). Full suite 419 green, zero warnings under -Werror, scalafmt clean.

Note for whoever closes P7.5: it is now fully subsumed and should be closed with a pointer here. Its own acceptance criterion — carry enough typed structure that the client can reconstruct the failure kind — is met on the client side; the agent still puts failure.toString on the wire (agent/SchedulerRequestHandler), which is a protocol-module concern for Phase E.
